what_happened: Discovered that check-module-invariants.sh's C16 blocks (both the FormalSystem-only half and the all-roots half) are RUN_BUILD-gated and CI invokes the script with --no-build, so flipping ENFORCE_C16_ROOTS=1 affects only the local full-mode gate, not CI; FormalSystem's own C16 enforcement in CI actually comes from the separate lean-action lint:true step via lake lint/nolints.json. Recorded as a risk/decision point in the research report so the plan phase does not assume local enforcement implies CI enforcement.

Confirmed via the vendored Batteries runLinter.lean source that scripts/nolints.json is read unconditionally at a fixed relative path regardless of which module is passed to runLinter, meaning the C16-roots baseline can reuse the existing nolints.json grandfathering mechanism directly (extend it with the other 16 dirty roots' findings, then flip ENFORCE_C16_ROOTS) rather than inventing a parallel per-root baseline file.

Dispatch description's 62 STALE DATE figure is the default-root (FormalSystem-only) measurement; CI invokes readme-lint.sh with 'FormalSystem BimodalTools', which measures 63 stale / 86 READMEs. Not a drift in the signal, a scope mismatch in the carried figure. Plan now requires a path-keyed baseline so one committed file serves every root subset, and records both measurements.

All five cheap-to-verify dispatch figures (62/4/84 READMEs; C20's 10, 145-of-1030, 39, 30) re-confirmed live this dispatch rather than carried: readme-lint.sh took seconds and check-module-invariants.sh --no-build ran detached while the plan was authored, exiting 0. The 18-root C16 denominator was independently re-derived from scripts/lake_targets.py. Only the 231/16 numerator remains carried, and Phase 3 measures it as its first task.
